**STRICTLY PRIVATE AND CONFIDENTIAL – WITHOUT PREJUDICE**

---

[Company Letterhead]

Date: [insert date]

To,
The Legal Department / Authorised Representative
Acme Components Ltd
[Insert address of Acme Components Ltd]

---

**Re: Your Legal Notice Ref. ACM/LGL/2026/114 dated 2 November 2026 – Invoice No. 4471**

Dear Sir / Madam,

We write on behalf of our client, **[insert full legal name of recipient company]** ("our Client"), in response to the legal notice bearing your reference **ACM/LGL/2026/114**, dated **2 November 2026** ("the Notice"), issued by Acme Components Ltd ("your Client") in connection with Invoice No. 4471 and a demand for payment of **INR 15,00,000**.

Receipt of the Notice is acknowledged. Our Client disputes neither the fact of receipt nor the existence of a commercial relationship with your Client. All rights are expressly reserved.

---

**Response to Substantive Allegations**

**1. Alleged Outstanding Amount of INR 15,00,000 (Invoice No. 4471)**

The Notice demands payment of INR 15,00,000 purportedly due under Invoice No. 4471. Our Client is currently conducting a thorough internal review of its records in relation to this invoice, including but not limited to the underlying purchase order(s), delivery documentation, contractual terms governing payment, and any prior correspondence between the parties. Accordingly, this allegation is **under review**. No admission is made, whether express or implied, as to the validity, accuracy, or enforceability of the claimed amount.

**2. Alleged Entitlement to Payment Within 15 Days**

The Notice asserts that payment of the claimed sum is due within 15 days of receipt. Our Client notes that the contractual terms and conditions governing the parties' arrangement, including any agreed payment timelines, are subject to the same internal review referenced above. No concession is made as to the existence of any obligation to make payment within the timeframe stipulated in the Notice, or at all at this stage.

**3. Further Allegations / Supporting Particulars**

The Notice does not, as presently constituted, set out with sufficient particularity the basis upon which the sum of INR 15,00,000 is claimed — including, for example, [confirm whether supporting documents such as delivery receipts, signed acknowledgements, or prior payment history were enclosed with the Notice]. Our Client reserves the right to seek further particulars and supporting documentation in order to conduct a complete and fair assessment of your Client's claim.

---

**Reservation of Rights**

Nothing in this letter constitutes an admission of liability, an acknowledgement of any debt, or a waiver of any right, defence, or remedy available to our Client, whether in law, equity, or contract. All such rights are expressly and unconditionally reserved.

---

**Next Steps**

Our Client is committed to engaging with this matter in good faith. We anticipate being in a position to revert with a substantive response following the conclusion of the internal review referred to above. We would request that your Client extend reasonable time for this purpose and refrain from initiating any further proceedings in the interim.

We invite your Client to provide, at the earliest opportunity, complete copies of all documents relied upon in support of the claim, including Invoice No. 4471, the relevant purchase order(s), proof of delivery, and any applicable contractual terms.

Yours faithfully,

**[Name of Lawyer / Authorised Signatory]**
**[Designation]**
**[Law Firm Name / Company Name]**
**[Contact Details]**

---

*This letter is written without prejudice to all rights and remedies of [insert recipient company name], all of which are expressly reserved.*

---

> **DRAFTING NOTE FOR REVIEWING LAWYER:** The following items require confirmation before this letter is finalised and sent:
> - Full legal name and registered address of the recipient company.
> - Full address of Acme Components Ltd for service.
> - Whether any supporting documents (delivery receipts, purchase orders, etc.) were enclosed with the Notice — the draft flags this as a placeholder at paragraph 3.
> - Whether the internal review has surfaced any factual basis to positively rebut the claim; if so, those facts should be inserted in place of the "under review" notation.
> - Whether the response deadline of 17 November 2026 can be met, or whether an extension should be sought proactively.
> - Applicable governing law and jurisdiction, if relevant to the response.
